capabilities: Encrypt secret fenced blocks and inline code spans with AES-256-GCM via a passphrase prompt
Reveal, copy, or edit decrypted secrets in place in Live Preview and reading view
Manage multiple session passphrases and reuse or re-lock secrets with their original key
Decrypt all secret-lock blocks in a note or forget all stored passphrases via commands
disambiguation: Not a password manager; it only encrypts secrets inside note files, and the README recommends a dedicated password manager if audited crypto is required.
extras: README includes an explicit threat model: plaintext can remain in undo history, File Recovery snapshots, sync version history, and filesystem backups; there is no passphrase recovery, the crypto is unaudited, and the key picker leaks the first and last character of each passphrase. Manual install only; no marketplace or sync of any state.
motivation: The README motivates it by the risk of secrets sitting in plaintext when the vault is read by sync services, backup tools, or AI agents.
problem: Vault files are plain Markdown, so passwords and tokens stored in notes are readable by sync services, backups, and AI agents that crawl the vault.
summary: Encrypts fenced code blocks and inline code spans containing secrets with AES-256-GCM so plaintext never sits in the note file.
